question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus washout with persistence tracking
ideas.description: Induce AP-1 activity with a controlled stimulus or an inducible Fos/Jun system, then withdraw it and track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac, and target-gene expression over days. Memory is supported if these marks and transcripts stay elevated after AP-1 activity returns to baseline, and decay kinetics can be compared with control sites.

ideas.title: Rechallenge test for primed responses
ideas.description: Compare first and second exposures to the same stimulus after a rest period, measuring the speed, amplitude, and AP-1 target-gene induction in each. Repeating this in Fos or Jun knockout and dominant-negative cells tests whether AP-1 is required for the faster, stronger secondary response.

ideas.title: Causal dissection of AP-1 motifs at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Identify enhancers that stay open after washout, then use CRISPR base editing or saturation mutagenesis to disrupt their AP-1 motifs. Check whether accessibility persistence and faster re-induction are lost, and use dCas9-based epigenetic editing to test whether AP-1 binding alone is sufficient to restore the memory signal.

ideas.title: Mapping AP-1 occupancy versus epigenetic retention over time
ideas.description: Run CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq for c-Fos and c-Jun alongside histone marks across a stimulation and washout time course. This shows whether memory is carried by retained histone marks after AP-1 has left the chromatin (bookmarking), or whether AP-1 must rebind at each re-exposure.

ideas.title: Single-cell live reporting of activation history across divisions
ideas.description: Use a destabilized fluorescent reporter driven by the Fos promoter, with live imaging and lineage tracking, to record each cell's prior activation history. Test whether past AP-1 activity predicts future response in the same cell and whether that history is inherited by daughter cells, which would distinguish cell-intrinsic memory from population-level effects.
